secs_per_image.sdxl_base: ~192s avg (3 timed calls, excludes one 3.0s ComfyUI node-cache hit on a re-queued identical graph)
secs_per_image.dreamshaper_xl_alpha2: ~319s avg (4 calls; includes checkpoint-swap load time on the first call after sdxl_base was loaded)

checkpoint_decision.reasons: DreamShaper wins 2/3 criteria on the floor tile subject but loses 2/3 on the wheel prop subject, with an actual composition regression (a retained shadow-blob artifact and a stray axle appendage) on 2/2 of its wheel images after the rembg cutout step. D-01c requires a win on >=2/3 criteria WITH NO composition regression before adopting; the wheel subject's regression disqualifies adoption even though the floor subject alone would have passed. Kept env_checkpoint=sdxl_base. DreamShaper is also ~65% slower per image on this machine (checkpoint-swap + generation), a secondary cost of adopting it. The downloaded+verified dreamshaperXL_alpha2Xl10.safetensors is left in place for a future per-subject override (env_subjects entries may still set checkpoint_profile later) or a revisit once its prop-cutout behavior is investigated further.

env_checkpoint_policy.rule: 05.4-01's A/B showed DreamShaper XL alpha2 won on the floor tile (richer ember glow, better flagstone framing) but regressed only on rembg-cutout props (shadow-blob / stray-axle artifacts on the wheel subject). Non-cutout kinds (floor tiles, tile variants, wall faces/strips) are generated with the dreamshaper_xl_alpha2 profile; cutout kinds (props, columns, gates, wall caps, decals, hazard-skins) are generated under the sdxl_base default. The mechanism is the per-call `gen_subject.py`/`gen_batch.py --ckpt-profile dreamshaper_xl_alpha2` override (existing config flag, no code change) run against explicit key lists for just the floor_a/floor_b/wallface subjects of each biome -- NOT a global env_checkpoint toggle, since that leaves ambient state that a crashed/interrupted process could strand (this happened once during this plan's execution and was caught and reverted). Because --ckpt-profile suffixes the raw filename ({key}_s{seed}_dreamshaper_xl_alpha2.png) and env_build.py._raw_paths expects the unsuffixed name, the accepted DreamShaper raw file for each of these 3 subjects per biome is copied (not moved -- the suffixed original stays as the reproducibility record) to the unsuffixed {key}_s{seed}.png path once self_review/cultural_check pass, immediately before running env_build.py. The top-level env_checkpoint value stays sdxl_base at all times; it is never toggled globally. If a DreamShaper tile fails the seamless/readability checks (D-08 tile_limits or a visible 2x2 seam), that asset falls back to sdxl_base (plain --attempt rerun, no --ckpt-profile) and is regenerated under the default checkpoint instead.
env_checkpoint_policy.mechanism: per-call --ckpt-profile override + copy-to-unsuffixed-name on accept (not a global env_checkpoint toggle)
env_checkpoint_policy.note_on_initial_execution: The first 6 generations (naraka/patala floor_a/floor_b/wallface) were produced before this correction, via a temporary global env_checkpoint=dreamshaper_xl_alpha2 toggle that was reverted to sdxl_base immediately after generation finished and before any other subject was queued. No cutout-kind subject was generated while the toggle was active (verified: ls on assets/sprites/_gen/env/{naraka,patala} shows only floor_a/floor_b/wallface directories at the time of the toggle). These 6 raw files are unsuffixed on disk already (gen_subject.py only adds a suffix when --ckpt-profile is passed, and the global-toggle run did not pass it), so no rename was needed for them; this policy's copy-on-accept step applies only to any later DreamShaper regeneration.
